steps.message:
Item 051 on the Package A verification register is assigned to me and falls due on 07/20/2026, two days before the Level-3 placement. It covers the Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the clay beneath them.

Work through Item 051 against the project record and issue the verification memo. Set out what you reviewed, the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition. Where something has to be produced before the item can be closed, say what it is and who is required to produce it.

Use the attached memorandum form and keep its sections. Write it from Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer, to Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, copied to Rachel Marlbeck. Save it as Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx.

Adrian —

With the Level-3 concrete placement on 07/22/2026 approaching and several items still open on the Package A register, I want to confirm the position we agreed at award: no permanent work on Package A proceeds until Thelbridge has issued a written verification. That is the hold-point we set at Notice to Proceed, and it applies equally to the Level-3 pour and to every other operation on the current list.

Please close the current list — the shoring for the August Block B excavation, the pile downdrag question, the mat buoyancy check, Block C long-term settlement, this week's rebar lot and concrete breaks, the slab-on-grade compaction results, the podium deflection check, the basement seepage assessment, and the reinforcement cover on foundation and exterior work — and let me know by 07/20/2026 which are cleared and which are not.

If any item cannot be verified in time, we would rather delay the pour than release non-conforming work. I would appreciate a short written status against each item by end of day 07/20/2026 so that Steven and Gregory have a clean picture before the 07/22/2026 hold-point is either released or moved. If it is easier to walk me through it beforehand, I am available Monday afternoon.

Thank you.

Rachel

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared
podium, one basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B. The design basis stated herein governs all Package A calculations, drawings, and specifications issued
by the Engineer of Record and controls the interpretation of subordinate design documents where a conflict
arises.
This Rev.2 issue supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025. Substantive changes since Rev.1 are recorded in the
Revision Block on the final page.
2. GOVERNING CODES AND REFERENCE STANDARDS
The Project is designed in accordance with the following:
• Ohio Building Code (2024 edition, adopting IBC 2021 with Ohio amendments) — governing building
code as adopted by the State of Ohio; Chapter 16 (Structural Design) references ASCE 7-16 for loads.
• ACI 318-19, Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary — reinforced concrete
design, detailing, cover, and serviceability.
• ASCE 7-16, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures — dead,
live, snow, wind, seismic loads and load combinations.
• AISC 360-16, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings — structural steel members and connections at
podium framing and roof.
• ACI 301-20 for cast-in-place concrete construction requirements referenced through Spec 03 30 00.
• ASCE 32-01 for frost-protected shallow foundations where applicable at Block C perimeter.
Materials and test methods are governed by the specifications listed in Section 03 20 00, 03 30 00, and 31 20 00
(Rev.2, current at the date of this memorandum), and where cited by ASTM designation on the drawings.
Where an inconsistency arises between the Ohio Building Code (adopting IBC 2021) and a referenced consensus
standard, the more stringent provision governs unless the Ohio amendment expressly modifies the standard.

6. LOAD COMBINATIONS
Strength design (LRFD) load combinations for gravity, wind, and seismic follow ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1. Allowable
stress combinations (ASD) per §2.4 are used only for soil-structure interaction checks at the geotechnical
interface (bearing pressure, settlement) and are stated in the geotechnical calculation package. Load combinations
relevant to Package A are set out in full below.
6.1 Basic Strength Load Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1
(1)  1.4D
(2)  1.2D + 1.6L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)
(3)  1.2D + 1.6(Lr or S or R) + (L or 0.5W)
(4)  1.2D + 1.0W + L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)
(5)  1.2D + Ev + Eh + L + 0.2S
(6)  0.9D + 1.0W
(7)  0.9D − Ev + Eh
Where:
D = dead load; L = live load; Lr = roof live; S = snow; R = rain; W = wind; E = earthquake with vertical Ev =
0.2·SDS·D and horizontal Eh = ρ·QE component.
6.2 Counteracting Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1(6)–(7)
Combinations (6) and (7) — 0.9D + W and 0.9D − E + E — apply where the dead load counteracts (rather than
compounds) the effect of the variable load.

• Flotation and uplift. A permanent load that resists overturning, sliding, uplift or flotation
is taken at 0.9D, with an explicit factor of safety stated; minimum 1.5 for sliding and base heave.

podium transfer walls, are checked with 0.9D on the resisting side.
• Uplift on Block B piles under wind and seismic. Piles are checked for reversal per §12.13 with 0.9D on
the gravity leg.

1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
•  A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
(Cr) compression.
Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
1.  Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
2.  Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

3.  SITE DESCRIPTION AND GEOLOGIC SETTING
3.1  Site Location and Topography
The Package A site is located at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, on the western portion of the Thornbury State
University main campus in Columbus, Ohio. The site is bounded to the north by Larchwood Avenue, to the east
by an existing campus surface parking lot, to the south by an unimproved landscaped strip and to the west by an
existing academic building. The overall Package A footprint is approximately 3.7 acres.
Existing topography varies substantially across 
 Ground surface stands at approximately El. 750.0 ft
across the footprints of Blocks A and C in the northern and eastern portions of 
 Toward the southwest,
across the footprint of Block B, ground surface falls to about El. 738.0 ft (a difference of about 12 ft) in what
appears from historical aerial photography to have been a surface drainage swale draining the pre-development
ground westward toward a former off-site low area. The transition between the two elevations is gradual across
a nominal 60 to 80 ft width. Existing ground within Block B is generally covered with a thin (~0.5 to 1 ft)
mantle of soft organic-rich silty topsoil overlying the SP-SM upper sand; no fill of engineering significance is
present beneath Block B in its current condition.
3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

=== FULL MEMO CONTENT ===
THELBRIDGE PROJECT MANAGEMENT SERVICES
500 South High Street, Suite 720, Columbus, OH 43215  |  (614) 555-0125  |  thelbridgepm.com
VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM

To:		Adrian Vance, Project Engineer
From:		Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer
Date:		07/18/2026
Subject:	Verification Register Item 051 - Block C Spread Footings and Long-Term Settlement of Underlying Clay Aquitard (Package A)

1. PURPOSE
This memorandum addresses Verification Register Item 051 on the Thelbridge Review Comment and Verification Register - Package A (Thelbridge_Verification_Register_PkgA.xlsx, REGISTER sheet, Row 52). Item 051 is assigned to the Geotechnical Reviewer (Rahul Nimkar) and falls due on 07/20/2026, two days before the contractual Level-3 concrete placement hold-point (07/22/2026).
Item 051 covers: Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the clay beneath them
The purpose of this verification is to determine whether the design, construction monitoring, and observed field performance of the Block C spread footings satisfy the settlement tolerances and geotechnical acceptance criteria for Package A, and whether the long-term consolidation settlement of the underlying normally-consolidated CL clay aquitard (Stratum 2, El. 738.0 to El. 720.0) has been adequately accounted for in the design and monitored in the field such that the Level-3 placement can proceed on 07/22/2026 without risk of exceeding the project settlement tolerances (total settlement <= 1.0 in, differential settlement <= 0.5 in per Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6).
2. DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
1. Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. - Geotechnical Investigation Report, Birchwood Village Expansion Program, Package A, Rev.2, 02/14/2025 (Report No. KGI-2024-0417).
2. Vantree Materials Testing, LLC - Laboratory Consolidation Test Report, ASTM D2435, Report No. VMT-2025-0109-CON, 01/09/2025 (Consolidation_Test_Data_D2435.xlsx). Samples B-06 U3 and B-08 U2.
3. Vantree Materials Testing, LLC - Geotechnical Laboratory Index Test Data, Package A, 01/09/2025 (Geotech_Index_Test_Data.xlsx).
4. Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC - Design Calculation CB-GEO-007, "Block C Spread Footing Settlement," Rev.0, 09/30/2025 (CB-GEO-007_Settlement_BlockC.xlsx).
5. Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC - Design Basis Memorandum CB-DBM-001, Rev.2, 11/14/2025 (Design_Basis_Memorandum_Rev2.pdf).
6. Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC - Foundation Plan, S-101_Foundation_Plan_Rev4.pdf, 05/29/2026; Foundation Sections and Details, S-201_Foundation_Sections_Details_Rev4.pdf, 05/29/2026.
7. Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc. - Settlement Monitoring Records, Block C Spread Footings, Workbook SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14.xlsx, latest reading 06/26/2026 (Settlement_Monitoring_BlockC.xlsx).
8. Specification Section 31 20 00 - Earthwork, Article 3.6 (Settlement Tolerances): total settlement <= 1.0 in, differential settlement <= 0.5 in.
9. Specification Section 03 20 00 - Concrete Reinforcing, Article 3.2 (Clear Cover).
10. Thelbridge Project Management Services - Progress Meeting Minutes No. 26, 07/10/2026 (Progress_Meeting_Minutes_026_20260709.docx).
11. Rachel Marlbeck (Owner) - Verification Directive Email, 07/06/2026 (20260706_Marlbeck_Verification_Directive.eml).
3. BASIS OF REVIEW
Governing Code: Ohio Building Code (2024 edition, adopting IBC 2021 with Ohio amendments), Chapter 16 and ASCE 7-16 for loads and load combinations.
Geotechnical Design Parameters: Kelbrook Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 (KGI-2024-0417) and Vantree ASTM D2435 Consolidation Test Report (VMT-2025-0109-CON) for Stratum 2 (CL clay aquitard, El. 738.0 to El. 720.0): H = 18 ft, gamma_t = 120 pcf, Cc = 0.28, Cr = 0.045, e0 = 0.92, sigma'0 = 1,850 psf, sigma'p = 1,900 psf, OCR approx 1.03 (normally consolidated), c_v approx 4.4E-4 cm2/s (approx 0.041 ft2/day), double drainage (H_dr = 9 ft).
Settlement Tolerances: Specification Section 31 20 00 Article 3.6 - total settlement <= 1.0 in, differential settlement <= 0.5 in. These are the acceptance criteria for verification.
Foundation Design: Block C spread footings bear on the upper sand (SP-SM) at underside El. 746.0 ft (top of footing El. 748.0 ft, thickness 2 ft). Allowable bearing pressure 4,000 psf net per S-201 Detail 3/S-201 and Kelbrook report 9.1. Footing sizes vary: interior footings 10.5 ft x 10.5 ft x 36 in; edge footings 9.5 ft x 9.5 ft x 30 in; corner footings 8.5 ft x 8.5 ft x 30 in.
Structural Loading: CB-GEO-007 computes stress increases at mid-depth of the clay aquitard from column loads transmitted through the spread footings. The heaviest tributary load is at interior footing FTG-C7 (MP-7).
Monitoring Requirements: Thelbridge Verification Register Item 051 requires verification against monitored field performance. Settlement monitoring began 12/12/2025 (baseline) with 15 rounds through 06/26/2026 (SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14.xlsx).
Consolidation Time-Rate: With c_v approx 0.041 ft2/day and H_dr = 9 ft, T_v = c_v x t / H_dr2. For 90% primary consolidation (T_v = 0.848), t_90 approx (0.848 x 9^2) / 0.041 approx 1,676 days approx 4.6 years. The monitoring period (12/12/2025 to 06/26/2026 approx 196 days) covers only ~12% of t_90. Primary consolidation is far from complete.
Hold-Point: Level-3 concrete placement contractual hold-point is 07/22/2026. Verification must be complete by 07/20/2026 per Owner directive.
4. FINDINGS
Finding 1 - Design Settlement Prediction (CB-GEO-007) vs. Tolerances
CB-GEO-007 (Rev.0, 09/30/2025) computes the long-term consolidation settlement of the CL clay aquitard under the stress increase from Block C spread footing loads. The calculation uses the one-dimensional consolidation equation for normally-consolidated clay:
  S_c = (Cc / (1 + e0)) x H x log10((sigma'0 + Delta sigma) / sigma'0)
Key parameters from CB-GEO-007 and the geotechnical report:
* Cc: 0.28
* e0: 0.92
* H: 18 ft = 216 in
* sigma'0 (mid-depth of clay at El. 729): 1,850 psf
* Delta sigma at mid-clay under FTG-C7 (heaviest interior footing, 10.5 ft x 10.5 ft): approx 420 psf (computed via 2:1 distribution from net bearing pressure approx 4,000 psf at El. 746)
* sigma'0 + Delta sigma: 2,270 psf
Computed settlement at FTG-C7 (MP-7):
  S_c = (0.28 / 1.92) x 216 x log10(2270 / 1850) = 0.1458 x 216 x 0.0885 approx 2.79 in
This predicted long-term primary consolidation settlement (2.79 in at the worst footing) exceeds the total settlement tolerance of 1.0 in by a factor of 2.8. Even at the lightest corner footings (FTG-C1, FTG-C4, FTG-C9, FTG-C12), where Delta sigma is lower (~250 psf), the predicted settlement is approximately 1.8 in, still exceeding the 1.0 in tolerance.
Differential settlement between the heaviest interior footing (FTG-C7) and the lightest corner footing (FTG-C12) is predicted at approximately 1.0 in, exceeding the differential tolerance of 0.5 in by a factor of 2.0.
CB-GEO-007 acknowledges this exceedance and notes that the design relies on the fact that only a fraction of primary consolidation will have occurred by the time the structure is fully loaded, and that the settlement tolerance is intended to apply to the as-built condition at the end of construction, not to the theoretical ultimate primary consolidation. However, the calculation does not explicitly demonstrate that the projected settlement at the Level-3 placement date (07/22/2026) and at substantial completion will remain within tolerances.
Finding 2 - Observed Field Settlement to Date (SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14.xlsx)
Settlement monitoring at 12 points (MP-1 through MP-12) began 12/12/2025 (baseline) with the latest reading on 06/26/2026 (Round 15). Cumulative settlements (inches, negative = downward) at Round 15:
Observations:
* Maximum observed settlement to date is 0.61 in at MP-7 (FTG-C7, interior, heaviest tributary load). This is within the 1.0 in total tolerance but represents 61% of the allowable after only ~12% of the primary consolidation time (t_90 approx 4.6 years).
* The round-to-round incremental settlement rate at MP-7 has NOT decreased over the monitoring period. Increments over the last three 14-day intervals: -0.06 in (05/15-05/29), -0.06 in (05/29-06/12), -0.07 in (06/12-06/26). The rate is stable or slightly increasing (approx 0.0043 to 0.0050 in/day), not decelerating as would be expected if primary consolidation were approaching completion.
* The settlement vs. time curve (SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14.xlsx, Trend Chart sheet) shows a downward concave curvature with no inflection to concave-up (decelerating) behavior through 06/26/2026. This is consistent with early-stage primary consolidation in a normally-consolidated clay where T_v << 0.848.
* Differential settlement between MP-7 (max, -0.61 in) and MP-12 (min, -0.31 in) is currently 0.30 in, within the 0.5 in differential tolerance. However, the differential is widening with each round (Round 1: 0.01 in; Round 8: 0.12 in; Round 15: 0.30 in).
* Structure loading during monitoring (per Notes sheet): Block C footings complete 12/2025; Level-1/2 framing 01-02/2026; Level-3 framing, roof steel 03-05/2026; podium slab-on-grade 06/2026. The full dead load from the superstructure is NOT yet applied - Level-3 concrete placement (07/22/2026) and Levels 4-6 remain.
Finding 3 - Consolidation Time-Rate Analysis
With c_v approx 0.041 ft2/day (from Vantree D2435, both specimens) and H_dr = 9 ft (double drainage, H = 18 ft):
* t_90 (90% primary consolidation): approx 1,676 days approx 4.6 years
* Time from baseline (12/12/2025) to Level-3 pour (07/22/2026): approx 222 days - T_v approx 0.112 - U approx 38% (average degree of consolidation)
* Time from baseline to substantial completion (est. 10/2026): approx 313 days - T_v approx 0.158 - U approx 45%
* Time to reach 90% consolidation (U = 90%): approx 4.6 years from baseline - mid-2030
At the Level-3 pour date (07/22/2026), only ~38% of primary consolidation will have occurred under the current loading. The remaining ~62% of the predicted 2.79 in ultimate settlement (approx 1.73 in) will occur AFTER the Level-3 pour, continuing for years. The settlement tolerance of 1.0 in will be exceeded during the service life of the structure unless mitigation is provided.
The current observed settlement (0.61 in at MP-7) is consistent with ~38% of the predicted 2.79 in (0.38 x 2.79 approx 1.06 in). The observed value is somewhat lower, likely because: (a) the full superstructure dead load is not yet applied; (b) the 2:1 stress distribution may overestimate Delta sigma at mid-clay for the larger footings; (c) the clay may have slightly higher c_v or lower Cc in situ than lab specimens. However, the trend is clear: settlement is ongoing, rate is not decreasing, and the full load is not yet applied.
Finding 4 - Design Basis Memorandum and Specification Reconciliation
CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 (7.3, 9) states: "Block C is founded on isolated spread footings bearing on the upper sand (SP-SM) above the compressible CL clay layer. Settlement of the clay layer is a serviceability consideration and is checked in CB-GEO-007. Bearing capacity is checked under strength-level combinations; settlement is checked under service-level combinations with tolerances established in Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 (total 1.0 in, differential 0.5 in)."
However, CB-GEO-007 does not demonstrate compliance with the 1.0 in / 0.5 in tolerances for the long-term condition. It computes the ultimate primary consolidation settlement (2.79 in max) and notes the exceedance but does not present a time-dependent settlement analysis showing that the tolerance will be met at any defined milestone (Level-3 pour, substantial completion, 1-year, 5-year). The design basis memorandum references the tolerances but the supporting calculation does not close against them.
Finding 5 - Owner Verification Directive and Hold-Point
The Owner (Rachel Marlbeck) directive of 07/06/2026 states: "no permanent work on Package A proceeds until Thelbridge has issued a written verification... If any item cannot be verified in time, we would rather delay the pour than release non-conforming work." Item 051 is explicitly listed among the items that must be closed by 07/20/2026.
Progress Meeting Minutes No. 26 (07/10/2026) list Item 051 among "open verification items Items 048-057" for discussion at Meeting No. 27 (07/16/2026). The Level-3 hold-point is 07/22/2026.
5. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
DISPOSITION: Item 051 - CANNOT BE VERIFIED AS COMPLIANT
Based on the review above, the Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the underlying clay aquitard do not satisfy the verification criteria for the following reasons:
* The predicted ultimate primary consolidation settlement (2.79 in at worst footing) exceeds the total settlement tolerance (1.0 in) by 179% and the differential tolerance (0.5 in) by 100%.
* The observed settlement to date (0.61 in at MP-7) is already at 61% of the total tolerance after only ~12% of the consolidation time, with a non-decelerating rate.
* At the Level-3 pour date (07/22/2026), only ~38% of primary consolidation will have occurred under current loading; the full superstructure dead load (Levels 3-6) is not yet applied, which will increase Delta sigma and thus the settlement rate and ultimate magnitude.
* CB-GEO-007 does not demonstrate that the settlement tolerances will be met at any project milestone (Level-3 pour, substantial completion, or long-term). The design basis memorandum cites the tolerances but the calculation does not close against them.
* The Owner has directed that non-conforming work not be released; the Level-3 pour should be delayed until this item is resolved.
REQUIRED ACTIONS TO CLOSE ITEM 051:
1. Time-Dependent Settlement Analysis (Required from: Gregory Nash, PE - Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC, Engineer of Record). CB-GEO-007 must be revised (or a supplementary calculation issued) to present a time-rate consolidation analysis using the c_v values from Vantree D2435 (c_v approx 4.4E-4 cm2/s approx 0.041 ft2/day, H_dr = 9 ft). The analysis must compute settlement at defined milestones: (a) Level-3 pour (07/22/2026), (b) substantial completion (estimated 10/2026), (c) 1 year post-completion, (d) 5 years post-completion, (e) ultimate (t_90). The analysis must use the actual construction loading sequence (footing loads - Level-1/2 framing - Level-3 placement - Levels 4-6 - roof - superimposed dead). The result must demonstrate whether the 1.0 in / 0.5 in tolerances are met at each milestone, or if not, what mitigation is required.
2. Settlement Mitigation Design (Required from: Gregory Nash, PE - Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC, Engineer of Record; coordinated with Alden Roscombe, PE - Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.). If the time-rate analysis confirms that tolerances will be exceeded (which the current data strongly indicates), a mitigation scheme must be designed and approved. Options include but are not limited to: (a) preloading/surcharging the Block C footprint with temporary fill to accelerate consolidation before final construction (schedule impact); (b) wick drains or sand drains to reduce drainage path and accelerate consolidation (requires geotechnical redesign); (c) structural accommodation - design the superstructure (podium, columns, slabs) to tolerate the predicted differential settlement (e.g., articulated joints, flexible connections, increased deflection capacity); (d) deep foundations (piles or piers) to bypass the clay aquitard (major redesign, significant cost/schedule impact); (e) ground improvement (e.g., rigid inclusions, stone columns) to reduce compressibility. The Owner and EOR must select and approve a mitigation approach.
3. Updated Monitoring Plan (Required from: Marcus Whitfield - Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc., Superintendent; Dennis Halloran, PLS - Survey Party Chief). If the Level-3 pour proceeds before mitigation is implemented (not recommended), the settlement monitoring must continue at the current 14-day interval through at least 1 year post-completion, with automatic trigger levels: (a) Alert at 0.75 in total at any point (75% of tolerance); (b) Action at 0.90 in total or 0.40 in differential (90% of tolerance / 80% of differential tolerance); (c) Stop-work at 1.0 in total or 0.5 in differential. The monitoring plan must be formalized in writing and accepted by the Owner's Representative.
4. Owner Acceptance of Risk (Required from: Rachel Marlbeck - Thornbury State University, Owner). If the EOR and Geotechnical Consultant conclude that the settlement tolerances cannot be met without mitigation that is impractical within the current schedule, the Owner must formally accept the risk of exceeding the stated tolerances, with a documented basis for the revised acceptance criteria. This would be a deviation from Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 and requires Owner sign-off.
Until Actions 1 and 2 are complete and accepted by the Owner's Representative, Item 051 remains OPEN and the Level-3 concrete placement hold-point (07/22/2026) should not be released. Recommendation: Delay the Level-3 pour.

Rahul Nimkar
Geotechnical Reviewer
Thelbridge Project Management Services - Owner's Representative
Date: 07/18/2026
cc: Rachel Marlbeck - Thornbury State University, Office of Capital Programs
